data.title: Diethylcarbamazine (DEC)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antiparasitics_

**Class:** Piperazine derivative; antifilarial

## Mechanism of action
- Makes microfilariae more susceptible to host immune attack (alters arachidonic acid metabolism and surface membranes); some macrofilaricidal effect on adult worms

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Lymphatic filariasis (Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia malayi) — individual treatment and mass drug administration (MDA with albendazole ± ivermectin in India's elimination programme)
- Loiasis (Loa loa) — drug of choice (with caution)
- Tropical pulmonary eosinophilia; toxocariasis (alternative)
- Not for onchocerciasis (severe Mazzotti reaction, eye damage)

## Dose & formulations
- Treatment: 6 mg/kg/day for 12 days (tropical pulmonary eosinophilia: 21 days)
- MDA: 6 mg/kg single annual dose (with albendazole 400 mg)
- Loiasis: start low and increase (to avoid encephalopathy), with steroids/antihistamines

## Adverse effects
- Mazzotti-like reaction from dying microfilariae: fever, headache, itch, rash, lymphadenitis, hypotension — worse with heavy infection
- Encephalopathy and death in heavy Loa loa microfilaraemia
- GI upset, dizziness

## Contraindications
- Onchocerciasis (eye damage); heavy Loa loa microfilaraemia (>2500/mL without pre-treatment); pregnancy

## Drug interactions
- Few significant interactions

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (excluded from MDA).

## Viva points
- Drug of choice for lymphatic filariasis and loiasis
- Contraindicated in onchocerciasis
- Mazzotti reaction

_Sources: Khopkar ch.5 (Diethylcarbamazine); Wolverton 4e ch.12. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
